content.overview: Article 12 defines 'the State' for the purposes of Part III. Fundamental Rights are primarily enforceable against the State as so defined. Whether a body is an 'other authority' under Article 12 is a fact-sensitive inquiry guided by instrumentality and agency tests developed in case law.

sections.heading: Textual function
sections.body: Article 12 includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India. Verify the exact official text.

sections.heading: Other authorities
sections.body: Bodies beyond the core organs of government may fall within Article 12 when they are instrumentalities or agencies of the State. Tests consider factors such as financial, functional and administrative control. Do not assume every public function or funded body is automatically the State.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: First question in every Part III petition: is the respondent the State under Article 12? Plead facts of control, composition, and function. Horizontal application against pure private actors is exceptional and must be supported by authority.
